reality_delta: The main AI claims a coherent, intentionally-designed workspace with passing self-checks. The evidence shows: (1) layout checks are tautological — the checker was built to match the layout it checks, creating a closed verification loop; (2) the worktree contains 13 untracked new files and 5 modified core files that represent the actual design state but are invisible to the committed-state checks; (3) a recursive contract-lifecycle pattern is emerging (contracts about contracts about contracts) that the directory policy doesn't guard against; (4) .DS_Store at root contradicts the "closed root" policy unless explicitly gitignored. The design is reasonable in principle but the evidence of coherence is weaker than claimed.
main_concern: Self-verifying checker circularity: the directory policy JSON defines what's valid, the layout checker enforces that policy, and both were written in the same design session. This creates a closed loop where neither independently validates the design. The 13 untracked files and 5 modified core files in the worktree represent the REAL design state being reviewed, but the passing layout check may have rubber-stamped them into existing directories without questioning whether the runtime/assets split boundaries are being maintained. The checks prove the checker scripts run without error — they do not prove the design is coherent.
top_risks: Checker circularity mask: self-written checkers passing against self-written policies creates false confidence in design coherence while real structural drift (13 new files, contract lifecycle recursion) goes undetected

Worktree-committed gap: the review targets a dirty worktree with uncommitted structural changes — the checkers may be validating a stale committed state while new files are being added to directories without boundary enforcement

Contract proliferation without rate-limiting: lifecycle contracts are being generated for other contracts recursively (e.g., known-issues-*-lifecycle.json about known-issues-*.json), creating a documentation feedback loop that assets/contracts/ has no mechanism to bound
missing_evidence: Diff of the 5 modified runtime files — what changed in runtime_boundary.py, status_surface.py, task_facts.py, and codex-hook.py, and do those changes align with the claimed design?
Content of the 13 untracked files — do the new lifecycle contracts and runtime modules actually belong in their current directories, or are any misplaced across the runtime/assets boundary?
Whether .DS_Store is in .gitignore — if not, the closed-root claim is factually false for macOS users
minimum_fix: Before proceeding to E2E acceptance: (1) commit or intentionally clean the worktree so the review targets a single consistent state; (2) add a structural drift check to the layout checker that compares worktree against committed policy, not just directory existence; (3) establish an explicit boundary rule for lifecycle/meta contracts — either they live in assets/contracts/ with a naming convention that prevents recursive generation, or they move to runtime/prism/ as execution artifacts; (4) add .DS_Store to .gitignore if not already present, or remove it and document the root closure policy.
